Our online Baby and Child First Aid course was built by a former paramedic, so every topic is taught the way it actually unfolds at home: what you'll notice first, what to do straight away and when it's time to call 000.

Learn online at your own pace. Do it once and have knowledge for life 💜

No AI chat can prepare you for the moment your baby goes limp.
But training can.

Our paramedic-designed course teaches you the exact steps to take when every second counts. So you have practical knowledge you'll actually remember when the adrenaline hits.

The people who made this course have been there. They know what that moment feels like. And they built this so you're never in it without answers.

🕰️ 1 hour online
📢 100K+ parents trained
❤️ 10,000+ little lives saved

Let us teach you 💜

body.text:
Only 14% of Australian women have heard of CMV. It is the most common infection a baby can be born with.

Isla's mum was one of the 86%. Her family only found out when Isla did not pass her newborn hearing screening.

A few small changes at home can lower your risk. Our free guide covers what CMV is, the habits that matter and the questions to ask at your next appointment.

Download it free today 🩷

body.text:
Balloons are one of the leading non-food causes of choking in children.

A blueberry is firm, so the force of a back blow can shift it and pop it out. A piece of popped balloon is soft and thin. It moulds to the shape of the airway and seals it like cling wrap, and a back blow has almost nothing to grip onto.

At your next party, adults blow up the balloons, every popped piece gets picked up straight away, and foil balloons are the safer pick for the under fives 🎈

Our course covers the hazards most parents never think about, and exactly what to do if one gets past you 💜

text.title: Know the hazards. Know the fix.

body.text:
Some messages stay with you.

A mum who trained with us before her baby arrived shared what happened next. Watch to the end.

If you've been meaning to do your first aid course, let this be your reminder.

One hour online. Knowledge for life. 💜

Your mum did everything right in the 90s, the advice just changed after she did it.

Some of it was official guidance at the time, some of it was what every mum was told.

I’m a mum and a former paramedic and I’ve lost count of how many parents have told me the same thing. Their mum is about to babysit, they’re anxious about it and they don’t know how to bring it up.

Both of you want the same thing for the same little one, you’re just working from different editions.
Preventing it is one half. Knowing what to do in the seconds after is the other 💜

The first years of parenthood ask a lot, so we put every course we teach into one bundle.

Pregnancy through to kinder, online at your own pace with lifetime access ❤️

I was a paramedic for 8 years, and I drove as fast as I could in every emergency.

It still was not fast enough to be there for the part that matters. The first seconds of a choking or breathing emergency always belong to a parent, because nobody else can help faster than you.

In one hour online, you'll know exactly what to do while help is on the way 💜

When something goes wrong, your little one will not look for the door, or the phone, or the ambulance. They will look at you.

What they see in your face in that moment comes down to one thing: whether you were taught what to do before you needed it.

One hour online with a former paramedic, and the face they see is calm 💜 Let us teach you.

Every parent has been there, phone brightness turned right down, scrolling forums while your little one sleeps hot beside you.

The hours add up, and so does the worry. One hour with a former paramedic gives you a clear way to read what you're seeing, so you know when to keep watching and when it's time to get help 🤍

Parents save lives. Not paramedics.

I've seen this first hand in my time as a paramedic and this is why I created Tiny Hearts. I wanted to help parents before the emergency ever happened.

By the time we reach your front door, the most important minutes have already passed. What happens in them comes down to one thing: whether someone in the room knows what to do.

That someone is you.

Our Baby and Child First Aid course gives you the skills and the confidence to act when it matters most. One hour online, and you'll never wonder if you'd know what to do.

Kody's mum wasn't there. It was just Kody and his dad on a quiet morning before nap time, when he turned around and saw something wasn't right.

They had done our course together, so when it mattered, he knew exactly what to do and he saved his little boy's life 🤍

The person with your little one when something happens might not be you. One hour online, and everyone who loves them can be ready.

Respiratory distress often starts quietly, and the clues are in how hard your little one's body is working rather than how unwell they look, which is why so many parents only spot it once it's well underway.

Our online Baby and Child First Aid course shows you what to look for on real babies, so when the next cold comes through the house you can tell the difference between what you can keep an eye on at home and when it's time to act 🤍

You'll never plan to be in an emergency with your child. But you can decide now whether you'll know what to do when you are.

That decision takes one hour.

You'll learn how to spot the signs, how to act, and exactly what to do before help arrives.

Let us teach you ❤️

Living a long way from the nearest town shouldn't mean going without the skills to look after your little one in an emergency.

Our Baby and Child First Aid course is online, so you can do it from the couch while bub sleeps, at your own pace, wherever you are in Australia, and come back to it any time you want a refresher.

It's built from my years as a paramedic, so you can feel calm and ready in those first minutes before help arrives 🤍

No one ever thinks it'll be them. But when I was a paramedic, every single shift, it was someone who had woken up expecting a completely normal day.

A little one running around, watching TV or eating their lunch, and a minute later their whole world looked different. That's what the road taught me: we never know which ordinary day changes everything.

You don't have to live through one to know what to do in it. One hour online, and you'll have the knowledge for life 💜
